definition-changed.flag: alphanumeric coded character set; national coded character set
definition-changed.answer: §2002:4 gives both definitions ('...usage display and alphanumeric literals'; '...data items described as usage national and for national literals') in the same words as §2023:3.10 and 3.125. The obligation, 'associating each character with an ordinal position within the character set', has the same object in both editions, and the twin goldens pass at --std 2002.

definition-dropped.flag: character | in a coded character set (newer: undefined); character | in a screen item (newer: undefined); character | in cobol character repertoire (newer: undefined); character | in computer storage (newer: undefined); coded character set (newer: undefined); native national coded character set (newer: undefined)
definition-dropped.answer: §2002:4 defines the four senses of character (for example 'A code value that constitutes the coded representation of a letter') and coded character set ('A set of unambiguous rules that establishes a character set', after ISO/IEC 10646-1); 2023 uses the same notions without defining them. §2002:4 defines native national coded character set as 'The computer's national coded character set', which is what 2023's undefined use means. The ordinal-position obligation therefore covers the same two sets, and the dropped definitions do not change its scope.
